text:
Alex Kim: heads up — multiple customers reporting 5xx/gateway timeouts hitting /v1/generate since ~08:02 UTC. Tickets: #3421, #3423. Errors look like upstream cache failures in the runtime logs.
Sara Collins: seeing same from support queue. Most say timeouts, one reports 502 with 'upstream error'.
Alex Kim: pasted a snippet from runtime: ```2026-02-24T08:04:12Z runtime ERROR request_id=abc123 upstream_call failed: redis error: IOERR - Resource temporarily unavailable; fallback failed; responding 502```
Mateo Rivera: that IOERR string lines up with Redis client returning connection errors. I just checked infra -> redis-primary.*: high connection count and a handful of OOM eviction spikes around 08:00.
Jordan Lee: @Mateo can you confirm whether this is our managed Redis (cache cluster) or customer-supplied KV?
Mateo Rivera: it's our hosted prefix cache (redwood-prefix-cache) — multi-tenant Redis cluster we manage for hosted inference.
Priya Shah: Customer impact: increased latency, some requests hit 10s and then 502. Billing still counting tokens for attempts. Customers are annoyed. Any quick mitigation?
Mateo Rivera: immediate mitigations: 1) route requests to cache-bypass path (runtime supports CACHE=off per-request) 2) scale redis read replicas, or restart a flaky replica 3) enable degraded routing to cheaper model variant without cache dependency.
Alex Kim: can runtime team flip cache-bypass for all hosted API traffic as a short-term measure? We need to stop 5xx.
Mateo Rivera: I'll coordinate with @deploy-bot and @Jordan to flip a config. Will take 2–3m to propagate.
deploy-bot: action=switch-config user=Mateo Rivera target=runtime.global:cache_enabled value=false status=initiated
Jordan Lee: I'm seeing failing liveness probes on redis-replica-2 (OOMKilled last restart loop). Logs show authentication errors too: ```ERR Client sent AUTH, but no password is set``` which is weird — looks like config got rotated?
Priya Shah: could that auth message explain sudden connection failures? If the redis client retries with wrong auth, it'll get dropped.
Mateo Rivera: yes. Two things likely happened: (a) a config/secret for Redis password rotated incorrectly during a deploy, (b) high memory pressure triggered evictions and then restarts. Both would cause connection churn and IOERRs.
Sara Collins: customer-facing note: can we tell customers we have a cache service degradation causing 5xx and we're bypassing cache while we remediate? Need ETA.
Alex Kim: draft for status page: "We are experiencing degraded cache service impacting hosted inference leading to elevated 5xx/timeouts. We are temporarily bypassing prefix cache to restore availability. Engineers are investigating root cause (redis replica instability and possible secret rotation)." Thoughts?
Jordan Lee: add: "No model data loss; requests may be slower while cache is bypassed."
Mateo Rivera: Done — setting bypass now. deploy-bot: action=toggle-cache-bypass user=Mateo Rivera status=complete
deploy-bot: action=toggle-cache-bypass completed in 27s
Alex Kim: after bypass flip, saw immediate drop in 5xx from 18% to ~2% in last 5m. Latency rose ~120ms median, some p95 spikes but tolerable.
Priya Shah: reporting back to customers now; will include short repro steps so support can correlate.
Sara Collins: repro (non-destructive): ```curl -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate -H "Authorization: Bearer $API_KEY" -H "X-Request-ID: repro-123" -d '{"model":"gpt-xl","input":"hello"}' -v``` if you see a 502 with payload in logs with redis errors, it's the same. Also check runtime logs for "redis error" and "IOERR".
Mateo Rivera: longer-term fixes: 1) audit secret rotations to ensure redis password isn't rolled without coordinated runtime deploy. 2) add connection health circuit breaker in runtime so cache failures degrade faster to local compute rather than cascade. 3) increase replica count and memory headroom, add alert on AUTH errors.
Jordan Lee: I'll open infra ticket to pin the secret and replay the rotation audit (INFRA-881). Mateo, add a runtime PR for circuit-breaker (RUNTIME-412).
Alex Kim: any risk of billing disputes? Priya, talk to finance if customers want credits — but we should log token billing during errors.
Priya Shah: yes I'll flag for billing ops; we can offer credits case-by-case.
Sara Collins: final note: I'll close tickets with status "mitigated by cache bypass; root cause investigation ongoing" and link INFRA-881 + RUNTIME-412.
Mateo Rivera: follow-up checklist posted in incident doc: https://internal.redwood.ai/incidents/2026-02-cache-degrade (TODO: add telemetry graphs + redis SLOWLOG).
Alex Kim: thanks everyone. Will keep thread updated if replica comes back or if we need to roll restarts.
Mateo Rivera: replica restarted after manual eviction and the auth secret re-applied; we're running health checks. Observability shows connection error rate down to baseline. Will leave cache disabled until post-mortem conclusions.
Jordan Lee: last check: 5xx back to normal, p95 latency slightly elevated but within SLO. Reopen if regressions.
Sara Collins: closing support loop. :white_check_mark:
